notes: REVISED AMOUNTS NOW GROW LIKE THE REST OF THE PLAN. In v2026.11.11.01 to .03 a revised expense or contribution was a flat nominal figure, which silently stopped inflation on anything revised. Now newAmount is what is paid in the from month, and it steps up from there exactly as its base would: categories at the expense rate, contributions at the same rate only when growContributions is on, EMIs never (the app never inflates EMIs). One function, revisionAmountAt, prices every revised month for both the engine and the editor. Growth is read per calendar month through expGrowthAt, built on the same hikesForMonth rule as expGrowthMul. SCENARIO EDITOR DEFAULTS: picking an item and a month fills the amount box with what the projection has then, including earlier rows in the same scenario that are already in effect. The default follows target/month changes and edits to earlier rows until the user types in the box; after that it is never overwritten. An untouched default is dropped on save, because it equals what is already planned and grows the same way, so it changes nothing; the editor says so. PRE-EXISTING BUG FIXED, FOUND WHILE CHECKING DEFAULTS AGAINST THE SHEET: annual step-ups restarted at the start of the window being viewed. renderBudget calls runProjection with horizonStart set to the window start, and the step-up rule read that as the plan start. Opening the Projection sheet at Jan 2028 showed salary Rs 2,00,000 and rent Rs 42,405, missing the 2027 increases that every other page applies (correct: Rs 2,16,000 and Rs 44,949). The two annual-interest anniversary passes had the same fault, so a window starting in April or May would skip that May's FD/PPF credit. All three now anchor to the plan start via _growthAnchorYM. Verified old vs new sheet: windows Nov 26 to Oct 27 and May 26 to Apr 27 are identical row for row; Jan 28 to Dec 28 differs in 15 rows, all by the missing year of step-ups. Dashboard, Net Worth and Decisions are unaffected because they already started at the plan start. SECOND PRE-EXISTING BUG FIXED: the sheet's per-EMI row wrote e.amount into every active month and ignored Step up / down and pause events, while the engine charged the stepped amount. It now uses the shared emiScheduleFor. VERIFIED in headless Chromium: engine with no scenarios identical to v2026.05.13.03; 32 engine assertions pass, including growth after a revision and flat contributions when growth is off. 14 browser checks pass on the real editor and sheet: defaults equal the sheet cell for rent, a stepped EMI and an SIP; a later row's default includes an earlier row grown at the expense rate; with the scenario previewed, the sheet's Rent row plus revision row equals the default offered; sheet rent for Jun 28 is the same whether the window starts Jun 28 or Nov 26; no page errors. Chart.js stubbed. NOT VERIFIED: the guards sheetVsDash, decisionUsesChain, instrumentCrossPageMismatch and accountDeltaMismatches are not in the HTML file and were not run. The sheet still seeds account balances at the window start; that was not examined. KNOWN: Decisions itemisation lists only revisions that raise an expense. NOT BUILT: closed-EMI zero row; settlement on its own line; Edit balances port and Instruments page deletion; Decisions/Scenarios merge.
